gaps.discriminates: Definitively confirms or excludes thoracic aortic injury (rupture, pseudoaneurysm, intimal flap, containment) and distinguishes it from mimics like mediastinal hematoma from other sources (e.g., great vessel injury, esophageal rupture)

Differentiates compensated vs. decompensated shock — critical for distinguishing contained aortic injury (often normotensive/hypertensive early) from exsanguinating rupture or cardiac tamponade (hypotension, narrow pulse pressure, PEA)

Helps exclude acute coronary syndrome or pericarditis as causes of chest pain/dyspnea, and detects PEA precursors (e.g., electrical alternans, low voltage) suggestive of tamponade or massive mediastinal hemorrhage
